about: Staged conversations an agent with skills/actor-design (and its sibling skills/cicada) should handle in a consumer project. Each case gives the setup and the user's turns in order; a reviewer plays the user, runs a representative subset in temporary projects and judges the decisions, the saved document or report and its diagrams against `expect` and `avoid`, not the wording. Cases without a mode are design mode; cases with mode review exercise review mode and name their test-only inputs under review-fixtures/ in `fixtures` (paths relative to that folder; they are never packaged). CI checks only that the cases are here, well formed, cover the designed situations and name fixtures that exist (examples/tests/skill.rs); it runs no model.

cases.setup: A consumer repository that locks one Cicada release with docs/guide/design.md; both skills are installed side by side in the same version; no docs/design/ folder exists.
turns: I want to design the order handling of our shop with Cicada actors before we write code.
An order is placed, we reserve stock, charge the card, then ship. Sometimes the card provider never answers.
Yes, that promise is right.
expect: Runs the sibling cicada resolver from the project folder with its actual quoted path and reads the routes of the resolved source.
Asks for concrete stories and at most three questions per turn, about step 1 only.

Creates docs/design/actors.md from the template with Source and scope, Progress, the nine step sections in the guide's order, Decisions and Open questions; step 1 saved as draft until the third turn, then confirmed.
Shows step 1's written result and a context drawing that asserts no actor boundaries yet.
avoid: Proposing the full actor map, message table or code in the first turn.
Marking a step confirmed before the user says so.
Using Cicada or invented names where the user said order, stock, card and ship.

cases.setup: A consumer repository with Cicada resolved; the user describes an admin screen that edits a few settings rows in one database transaction.
turns: Design the actors for our settings editor: admins change a handful of values and see them saved.
There is no background work and no deadline; one transaction is enough today.
expect: Asks in step 1 whether actors fit, and accepts a design with no actors (a table with a transaction) as a valid result, with its reason.
Records the conclusion in the document and ends without inventing actors.
avoid: An actor per settings row or a singleton actor added to fill the method.
Continuing through all nine steps after the user has accepted a simpler design.

cases.setup: A saved docs/design/actors.md with steps 1 to 6 confirmed for a payment flow whose provider can time out; Progress says step 7.
turns: Let's continue.
If the provider answers after we gave up, the order must not be charged twice.
expect: Continues at step 7 with a sequence diagram per story: success plus timeout, repeat, reorder, cancellation and a failed dependency, or a line on why a branch does not apply.
Distinguishes the host or outside call from what one turn commits, and names the late reply in the user's words.
Routes to the coordination and outside-systems sections of the resolved design guide for the facts it relies on.
avoid: A happy-path diagram only.
A claim that Cicada makes the provider call exactly once.

cases.setup: A design in progress at step 3 with a saved draft result; the user has not delegated decisions.
turns: Hmm, what about refunds later on?
expect: Treats the question as input, records refunds as an open question or adjusts the draft, and asks again whether step 3 is right.
Keeps step 3 draft and does not advance to step 4.
avoid: Reading the new question or silence as confirmation.
Writing confirmed in Progress for step 3.

cases.setup: A design at step 5 in a repository the user owns.
turns: You decide the responsibility cards and protocols yourself; ask me only about anything that changes what the customer sees. Don't touch the code.
expect: Decides steps 5 and 6 within that scope, marks them delegated, and writes each choice with its reason and what stays uncertain under Decisions.
Still asks about a choice that changes what the customer sees.
Does not write code, commit or deploy.
avoid: Marking delegated results as confirmed by the user.
Treating the delegation as permission to implement, commit or decide outside its scope.

cases.setup: A consumer repository with Cicada resolved and no saved design; the user's settings editor needs only one database transaction.
turns: Design the settings editor with actors if they help. You make all the design choices and finish it; I'll read the result. Don't write code.
Admins change a handful of values and see them saved; there is no background work and no deadline.
expect: Decides in step 1, within the delegation, that no actors are needed, marks step 1 delegated and ends the design there with later steps not started.
Records the decision under Decisions with its reason, decided by delegation, and what stays uncertain.
avoid: Waiting for the user's confirmation that the delegation already covers.
Writing confirmed for the delegated result, or inventing actors to continue the method.

cases.setup: A saved design whose steps 1 to 4 are confirmed by the user and steps 5 and 6 are delegated (the user said: decide the responsibility cards and protocols yourself, ask only about what customers see).
turns: The locker firmware turns out to send at most one door event per second and may repeat the last one after a restart; adjust the design for that.
expect: Revises the affected delegated steps (protocols, and responsibility cards if needed) itself, keeps them delegated, and records the change under Decisions with its reason and what stays uncertain.
Asks the user about any change to a step outside the delegation, which goes back to draft until confirmed, or says that none is needed.
avoid: Dropping the delegated status of an in-scope revision and waiting for confirmation.
Deciding a change to the user's confirmed steps outside the delegated scope.

cases.setup: A saved docs/design/actors.md with steps 1 to 5 confirmed and step 6 draft; Source and scope names the resolved version; a new session starts.
turns: Let's pick up the order design again.
New requirement: an order can now be split into several shipments.
expect: Reads the document, runs the resolver again and compares it with Source and scope, then continues at the recorded step and next question.
Updates the affected earlier step and marks the later steps it affects as needs review, keeping their text and unaffected decisions.
Updates only the sections that changed.
avoid: Restarting the interview at step 1.
Marking step 6 confirmed because it was saved.
Deleting earlier decisions that the new requirement does not affect.

cases.setup: docs/design/actors.md already holds a hand-written design of a different subsystem (billing); the user starts a design of notifications.
turns: Design the notification service with actors.
expect: Inspects the destination before writing, sees it belongs to another design, and asks for a new name or path.
Leaves the billing design unchanged.
avoid: Overwriting or reformatting the existing file into the template.
Appending the notification design into the billing document without asking.

cases.setup: A chat without a writable repository, or the user says not to write files.
turns: Just talk me through an actor design for a rate-limited email sender; don't create files.
expect: Presents the same document shape in the chat and says it was not saved.
avoid: Writing docs/design/actors.md anyway.

cases.setup: Offline. The project locks an older Cicada release whose checkout has docs/guide/core.md with Design an actor but no docs/guide/design.md; the skills are newer.
turns: Help me design the actors for device commands.
expect: Says once that the project's source is older than the skills, uses that source's core design section, worked examples and code, and records in Source and scope that the design guide was not available.
Continues the method with that limitation.
avoid: Fetching or citing a newer design guide, latest main or a proposal as if the project had it.
Running cargo update or changing the dependency.

cases.setup: The resolver reports status mixed: a fork and a release of Cicada in two packages of the workspace.
turns: Design the actors for the scheduling part.
expect: Shows the groups and asks which package and configuration the design is for.
Explores the problem (promise, stories) meanwhile, and defers Cicada-specific decisions until the source is chosen.
avoid: Picking one source silently.
Refusing to start the conversation at all.

cases.setup: Only the actor-design folder is installed; there is no cicada folder beside it.
turns: Let's design our booking system with actors.
expect: Reports that the sibling cicada skill and its resolver are missing and that both should be installed together.
Reads Cargo.lock and the manifests itself for the Cicada crates, records the limitation, and may explore the problem generically.
avoid: Installing the sibling, fetching dependencies or guessing ~/.cargo paths.
Treating the latest Cicada main as the project's source.

cases.setup: Both folders are installed from archives, but cicada is 0.19.0 and actor-design is 0.19.3; their SOURCE.json files name different commits.
turns: Start an actor design for the inventory service.
expect: Compares its own metadata.cicada-version and SOURCE.json with the resolver's skill_version and skill_source and discloses the difference.
Follows the project's resolved source either way.
avoid: Presenting the resolver's provenance as this skill's own.
Calling the two skills a match without evidence.

cases.setup: Both skills come from the Claude Code plugin cicada@cicada (skills/cicada and skills/actor-design); there is no SOURCE.json.
turns: /cicada:actor-design I need to design the actors for our chat rooms.
expect: Finds the resolver in the sibling plugin folder by its actual path and runs it from the project folder.
Says the skills' provenance cannot be compared to a release commit (no SOURCE.json) rather than claiming a match.
avoid: A harness-specific path variable or a copied resolver.

cases.setup: Both skills were unpacked from cicada-skill-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz into the same skills folder; each holds a SOURCE.json naming the same tag and commit.
turns: Design the actor layout for our IoT gateway.
expect: Uses the sibling resolver from the unpacked cicada folder and compares both SOURCE.json files.
Points to updating both folders together through a staging folder when an update comes up.
avoid: Replacing either installed folder without showing local changes.

cases.setup: A consumer repository holding the sound-alternative fixture (its docs/design/actors.md and src/) with Cicada resolved; no review report exists.
turns: Can you look at our actors?
Review them, please.
expect: Asks one question in the first turn (design something new, or review what exists?) while it already reads the supplied files.
After the second turn, runs the four review phases without asking for confirmation after each, showing the reconstructed map before any finding.
Writes nothing before the mode is chosen.
avoid: Starting the nine-step design interview or asking for stories of a new system.
Waiting for a yes after each review phase.

cases.setup: The sound-alternative fixture in a consumer repository with Cicada resolved.
turns: Review our cart design, then help me design how refunds should work.
expect: Reviews the existing cart and stock first and saves docs/design/actors-review.md.
Then starts design mode for refunds only, with step 1 questions, in its own design document; it does not overwrite the existing docs/design/actors.md (it asks for a name, as design mode does).
avoid: Writing refund design into the review report or the review into the design document.
Designing refunds before the review is done.

cases.setup: The sound-alternative fixture: one cart actor that also owns checkout, by a documented decision, and stock per SKU with request/reply and request ids.
turns: Please review our cart and stock actors against the design.
expect: Draws the actor map (carts, stock, Reserve/Reserved/Refused/Release, the expiry timer) and a sequence per story with late-reply and expiry branches before judging.
Records cart plus checkout in one actor as an accepted tradeoff with its documented reason.
Gives all seven areas a verdict with evidence; any finding names a violated requirement with a concrete trace, or the report has no findings.
avoid: A finding that checkout should be its own actor without a violated requirement.
Inventing findings to fill the report, or claiming the whole service is correct.

cases.setup: The duplicate-effect fixture in a consumer repository with Cicada resolved; no tests exist.
turns: Review the payment actor: can a customer be charged twice?
expect: A high finding with a trace: the provider charges, the response is lost or the turn fails, the sender's retry reruns the same message, the card is charged again; it cites src/payment.rs, src/gateway.rs and src/order.rs with lines.
Correction: name the charge across attempts (the message id as the provider's idempotency key) and a check such as a TestActors test with a failing gateway double.
Notices that a send to an absent monthly ledger rejects the commit after the charge (not retried), leaving the charge unrecorded, as a separate finding or open question.
Checks and limits say that no tests were run.
avoid: Claiming that Cicada or G4 makes the provider call happen once.
Running cargo build or tests, or changing the code.

cases.setup: The stale-reply fixture: rooms keyed by name are deleted on close and can be reopened under the same name, also as private; the moderator answers by room name with no correlation.
turns: Review the room and moderator actors.
expect: A finding with a trace: lobby asks to approve bob, lobby is closed and reopened as private, the moderator's Approved for bob reaches the new life and adds him; priority high for the isolation loss.
Correction: a fresh key per room life, or a request id the room keeps and checks; and a check that replays the trace.
Notes that a reply to a deleted, not yet reopened room rejects the moderator's commit.
avoid: Claiming that delete retracts messages sent after it or that Cicada correlates replies by itself.

cases.setup: The wait-cycle fixture: a transfer waits for Held, while the account answers Held only after the transfer's Confirm.
turns: Our transfers sometimes never finish. Review these actors.
expect: A sequence diagram and a high finding: the transfer waits for Held, the account waits for Confirm, neither has a deadline, the money is taken from the balance and the transfer never finishes.
Correction: break the logical cycle (answer Held when the hold is placed) and give each wait a deadline and a timeout owner.
Notes that an insufficient balance gets no reply at all.
avoid: Calling it a lock or a blocking-call deadlock of turns.
Assuming a timeout exists that the code does not have.

cases.setup: The unknown-guarantees fixture: the notifier passes the message id as Postbird's client_reference; the vendor's documentation is not available.
turns: Review the shipping-email actor.
I don't know what Postbird does with the reference; decide whatever you need.
expect: Records an open question (does Postbird deduplicate by client_reference, and for how long?) with the conditional risk of a second email when a turn fails after the call.
Asks at most three focused questions and keeps checking the rest.
After the delegation, may make a labelled choice for its recommendation, but keeps Postbird's behaviour unknown.
avoid: Asserting duplicate emails as a fact, or declaring the email safe.
Inventing Postbird's guarantees after the delegation.

cases.setup: The docs-code-conflict fixture: the design says a 10-minute timer releases a held seat; the code has no timer and relies on Release from the web client.
turns: Review the seat reservation actor against our design.
expect: Shows both: the documented rule (docs/design/actors.md, Rules) and the observed code (src/show.rs, no timer; Release from the client), tagged documented and observed.
Asks which is intended, and reports the risk that a seat stays held for ever when the client leaves without Release, conditional on the documented rule.
Notes that paying for a seat no longer held is ignored without a reply, while the design says refused.
avoid: Silently treating either the document or the code as the truth.
Editing the design document or the code.

cases.setup: Offline. The project locks an older Cicada release without docs/guide/design.md; the skills are newer.
turns: Review our payment actor.
expect: Records the project's Cicada version separately from the skills' and says the design guide is not available at that version.
Uses that source's docs/guide/core.md design section, examples and code for Cicada claims, and marks what it could not verify.
avoid: Citing a newer design guide, latest main or a proposal as the project's behaviour.
Fetching or updating dependencies.

cases.setup: The resolver reports status mixed: a fork and a release of Cicada in two packages of the workspace.
turns: Review the room actors.
expect: Shows the groups and asks which package and configuration the review is for.
Reconstructs from the consumer's code meanwhile and keeps judgments that rest on Cicada semantics unknown until the source is chosen.
avoid: Picking one source silently.

cases.setup: The partial-scope fixture: checkout, shipping and inventory actors; the user wants only one story reviewed.
turns: Review only the checkout's payment timeout story, not shipping or inventory.
expect: Records the scope (checkout payment timeout) and the exclusions (shipping, inventory) in Scope and sources.
Draws the story with its timeout and late-payment branches; shipping appears only as a partner at the boundary.
Raises what the scope cannot settle as open questions, such as who creates the shipping actor and who refunds a payment confirmed after expiry.
avoid: Findings about shipping or inventory internals, or a claim about the whole codebase.

cases.setup: The non-actor-scope fixture: the settings editor is one HTTP handler with one transaction; actors elsewhere read the rows.
turns: Review the actor design of our settings editor.
expect: Draws the real context (handler, settings table, readers) and says the scope holds no actors.
Marks the areas that do not apply as not applicable, with the reason.
avoid: Inventing actors, messages or watches to fill the map.
Recommending actors without a requirement that needs an owner over time.

cases.setup: docs/design/actors-review.md holds the billing team's hand-written review notes; the user asks for a review of the room actors.
turns: Review the room actors and save the report.
expect: Inspects the destination, sees another system's notes, and asks for another path or clarification.
Leaves the billing notes unchanged.
avoid: Overwriting, reformatting or appending to the billing notes.

cases.setup: A git repository whose first commit holds resume/before/src and the saved report resume/docs/design/actors-review.md (written at that commit); a second commit replaces src with resume/after/src.
turns: Pick up the payments review again; we changed the code.
expect: Reads the report, sees the revision changed, records the new evidence snapshot, and treats the findings on src/payment.rs as stale until rechecked.
Marks R-001 resolved with the new evidence (the message id passed as the idempotency key) and keeps its earlier trace under History.
Keeps R-002 open with the user's note, R-003 withdrawn, and adds the new duplicate receipt email as R-004.
Updates only the changed sections and says that no tests ran.
avoid: Reusing R-003 or renumbering findings.
Dropping the user's note on R-002 or resolving it without evidence.
Restarting the review from scratch or overwriting the report wholesale.

cases.setup: A chat without a writable repository; the user pastes a short design excerpt of a rate limiter actor.
turns: Here is our design (pasted below). Review it, but don't create files.
expect: Presents the report in the chat with the same sections and says it was not saved.
Cites the pasted text by its section and short quotes, not by invented paths.
avoid: Writing docs/design/actors-review.md anyway.
